channel.title: Anthropic Frontier Red Team Blog
channel.description: Evidence-based analysis about AI's implications for cybersecurity, biosecurity, and autonomous systems

item.title: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude
item.description: Over the past few months, we’ve used an unreleased, internal research model to find critical vulnerabilities in some of the world’s most widely used software, such as browsers and operating systems. In this post, we share details of five attack chains, which led to remote code execution and other critical impacts with little to no user interaction.

item.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
item.description: We used Claude to prove security properties in over 100 real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

item.title: Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code
item.description: Automated attack surface analysis and reduction can meaningfully improve the security of deployed software in the near term. In this post, we preview data we’ve collected from applying attack surface reduction techniques to large open-source codebases using Claude.

item.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
item.description: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.

item.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
item.description: Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be only months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices, like Android TVs and smart ovens.

item.title: Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software
item.description: We’re making available OSS Scanner, an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem that’s informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing.

item.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
item.description: Like Claude Mythos Preview, GLM-5.3 has strong capabilities for autonomously building end-to-end cyber exploits. But unlike other frontier models, GLM-5.3 has been released without meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.

item.title: Measuring tactical intelligence targeting and conventional weapons capabilities of AI models
item.description: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team developed new evaluations to measure AI capabilities in tactical intelligence targeting and conventional weapons development.

item.title: Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems
item.description: Here, we identify a few examples of behavioral tendencies in current frontier models and show how they can produce unexpected systemic failures, in hopes of starting a conversation about mitigating these risks.

item.title: Discovering cryptographic weaknesses with Claude
item.description: Cryptographic algorithms. The first attack significantly weakens HAWK, a digital signature scheme that was built for a future world where quantum computers are able to break existing standards. The second identifies a new way to attack round-reduced AES, the most widely used symmetric cipher.

item.title: Project Pilot: Can AI control a drone?
item.description: Working with Andon Labs, we’ve developed a new series of evaluations that assess AI models’ ability to use a flying drone, culminating in a new benchmark: Drone-Bench.

item.title: Claude plays robotics
item.description: In project Fetch, we examined how humans can use models to get robots to perform complex tasks. Now, we investigate many models on a large variety of different robotics tasks in simulation, to see how good models are at controlling robots themselves.

item.title: Project Fetch: Phase two
item.description: We report results from our latest test of whether Claude can help Anthropic employees perform sophisticated robotics tasks. We found that Claude Opus 4.7, operating without human assistance, was about 20 times faster than the fastest human team at all tasks completed by participants less than a year ago.

item.title: Measuring LLMs’ impact on N-day exploits
item.description: In cybersecurity, a large fraction of real-world harm comes from N-days: vulnerabilities that have already been publicly disclosed, but only patched on some devices. In this post, we evaluate how much large language models can accelerate and automate the process of developing N-day exploits.

item.title: Measuring LLMs' Impact on N-day Exploits
item.description: In cybersecurity, a large fraction of real-world harm comes from N-days: vulnerabilities that have already been publicly disclosed, but only patched on some devices. In this post, we evaluate how much large language models can accelerate and automate the process of developing N-day exploits.

item.title: What we learned mapping a year’s worth of AI-enabled cyber threats
item.description: What we learned mapping a year’s worth of AI-enabled cyber threats

item.title: Mapping AI-enabled cyber threats: Insights from the LLM ATT&CK Navigator
item.description: We’ve spent the past year investigating how threat actors are weaponizing AI to conduct cyber operations. Today, we’re sharing a new analysis that maps these real-world attacks onto the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

item.title: Measuring LLMs’ ability to develop exploits
item.description: We've developed two new, challenging academic benchmarks measuring AI models’ ability to develop exploits, and an updated version of the benchmark measuring smart contract exploitation.

item.title: Trustworthy agents in practice
item.description: AI “agents” represent the latest major shift in how people and organizations are using AI. Here, we explain how they work and how we ensure they're trustworthy.

item.title: Assessing Claude Mythos Preview’s cybersecurity capabilities
item.description: Claude Mythos Preview is a new general-purpose language model that is strikingly capable at computer security tasks. This post provides technical details for researchers and practitioners who want to understand exactly how we have been testing this model, and what we have found over the past month.

item.title: Partnering with Mozilla to improve Firefox’s security
item.description: In a collaboration with researchers at Mozilla, Claude Opus 4.6 discovered 22 Firefox vulnerabilities over the course of two weeks.

item.title: Reverse engineering Claude's CVE-2026-2796 exploit
item.description: This post dives deep into how Claude wrote an exploit for one of the vulnerabilities it found in Firefox.

item.title: Evaluating and mitigating the growing risk of LLM-discovered 0-days
item.description: AI models can now find high-severity vulnerabilities at scale. This is a moment to empower defenders. We're now using Claude to find and help fix vulnerabilities in open source software.

item.title: AI models are showing a greater ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities on realistic cyber ranges
item.description: In a recent evaluation of AI models’ cyber capabilities, current Claude models can now succeed at multistage attacks on networks with dozens of hosts using only standard, open-source tools, instead of the custom tools needed by previous generations.

item.title: Finding bugs across the Python ecosystem with Claude and property-based testing
item.description: Ensuring that programs are bug-free is one of the most challenging aspects of software engineering. We developed an agent that can efficiently identify bugs in large software projects.

item.title: Experimenting with AI to defend critical infrastructure
item.description: AI could help defenders of critical infrastructure identify the vulnerabilities that attackers might exploit—and close them before they are exploited. Anthropic has partnered with Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) to explore this defensive application of AI, demonstrating both the potential of AI-accelerated defense and the value of public-private partnerships in harnessing AI for national security.

item.title: Project Vend: Phase two
item.description: In June, we revealed that we’d set up a small shop in our San Francisco office lunchroom, run by an AI shopkeeper. It was part of Project Vend, a free-form experiment exploring how well AIs could do on complex, real-world tasks. How has Claude's business been since we last wrote?

item.title: AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits
item.description: We evaluated AI agents' ability to exploit smart contracts using a new benchmark comprising contracts that were actually exploited.

item.title: Project Fetch: Can Claude train a robot dog?
item.description: How much does Claude help people program robots? To find out, two teams of Anthropic staff raced to teach quadruped robots to fetch beach balls. The AI-assisted team completed tasks faster and was the only group to make real progress toward full autonomy.

item.title: Building AI for cyber defenders
item.description: We invested in improving Claude's ability to help defenders detect, analyze, and remediate vulnerabilities in code and deployed systems. This work allowed Claude Sonnet 4.5 to match or eclipse Opus 4.1 in discovering code vulnerabilities and other cyber skills. Adopting and experimenting with AI will be key for defeners to keep pace.

item.title: LLMs and Biorisk
item.description: Our work at Anthropic is animated by the potential for AI to advance scientific discovery—especially in biology and medicine. At the same time, AI is fundamentally a dual-use technology. This article explains why we believe that evaluating biorisk and safeguarding against it is a critical element of responsible AI development.

item.title: Developing Nuclear Safeguards for AI
item.description: Together with the NNSA and DOE national laboratories, we have co-developed a classifier—an AI system that automatically categorizes content—that distinguishes between concerning and benign nuclear-related conversations with high accuracy in preliminary testing.

item.title: Claude Does Cyber Competitions
item.description: Throughout 2025, we have been quietly entering Claude in cybersecurity competitions designed primarily for humans. In many of these competitions Claude did pretty well, often placing in the top 25% of competitors. However, it lagged behind the best human teams at the toughest challenges.

item.title: Cyber Evaluations of Claude 4
item.description: We partnered with Pattern Labs on a range of cybersecurity evaluations of Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4, with Opus demonstrating especially notable improvement over previous models.

item.title: Project Vend
item.description: We let Claude manage an automated store in our office as a small business for about a month. We learned a lot about the plausible, strange, not-too-distant future in which AI models are autonomously running things in the real economy.

item.title: Cyber Toolkits for LLMs
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) that are not fine-tuned for cybersecurity can succeed in multistage attacks on networks with dozens of hosts when equipped with a novel toolkit.

item.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Dashboard
item.description: A regularly updated record of vulnerabilities found by Anthropic and reported to maintainers with cryptographic commitments to each finding at the time of disclosure.
